segments.text: Hello Daniil, come in, have a seat. Where would you like to start today?
I don't know. My general practitioner suggested I come. She said I look exhausted and she's right.
How?
What does exhausted look like for you?
Like I'm running on fumes.
I work as a project manager at a logistics company and I've been completely burnt out since October.
Since October?
Did something happen then?
Not one thing.
We lost a big client, half of the team got moved on to the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.
Just never came back up after that.
What can they look for?
I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night.
Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.
That's a very long day. How was your sleep?
Terrible. Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.
I wake up at 3 and fall back asleep.
My head is dirt. Shipping schedules declined.
whether I've forgotten something.
Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.
And then?
Then I lie until about five and get up and make tea.
I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.
It sounds draining. Is there anything else going on in your life besides work?
Yeah, my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
That's a lot to carry alongside everything else. How is he?
Still himself, mostly.
His hands shake.
He's slower.
He gets frustrated.
He's having a drink and he's always being the strong one.
How are you involved in his care?
I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.
Neurology appointments are every few weeks.
It's about an hour each way.
Is there anybody who shares that with you?
Not really. My hungry sister Hannah lives in Toronto so all the care for our father falls on me.
How do you feel about that?
Guilty for even saying it. She calls him every Sunday. She's not the one who's neglecting him.
just I'm the one who's here.
Can you say more about the girl?
It feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who leaves cell.
So I don't say anything to anyone.
Not to Hannah either?
Just how I am, Lysifoyne.
What would be the point? She can't do anything from Canada.
But you want her to know if you said it.
That I'm not fine.
That someday they sit in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before you go in.
Because they can't face it.
That's an important thing to notice. What happens in those 10 minutes?
Nothing really. Just breathe. Look at our people going and everybody looks tired here.
You mentioned your GP. What did she say?
She did blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion if I asked about talking to someone.
She said I hadn't got time.
Yet you are here.
Girlfriend looked at, to be honest.
Claire.
She said she was done watching me disappear.
How is it with Claire?
She's very patient.
She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.
But I can see she's wearing a hat too.
In what way?
She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend
Because I always said no.
That's the thing I feel worst about, actually.
What stops you from saying yes?
The emails.
If I'm away, I'll come back to 200 of them.
That might need something.
So even rest has a price.
Yeah, exactly. Can't remember the last time I was properly off.
What did you do for yourself before October?
We ran.
I got me tears every Saturday morning.
We've done it for six years.
And now?
I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead. I just never went back.
How do you feel about it?
Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.
What would it mean to get some of that back?
A lot, probably. Just can't picture the time that would come from.
Leave this for a moment. What is your relationship with your boss like?
Peterson, he's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
What do you do when one arrives?
I answer it. Every time, even if I'm on bed. I hate it.
What I afraid would happen if you didn't answer?
Then he'd think I wasn't committed.
There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.
And did they did?
I don't know.
I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage.
Both things can be true.
Suppose so. I never said that I would have told.
Who are you, Moose, apart from the tiredness?
A lot, mostly.
Inheritable.
I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes.
What was happening for you in those minutes?
Heart was going and my hands were shaking.
He thought for a second it was a hard day, but it had passed.
Has it happened before?
Couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.
That sounds frightening.
It was. I hadn't told anyone about it, not even Claire.
Thank you for telling me. What are you afraid it means?
That I'm losing it.
I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.
Have you noticed anything that makes it worse?
Coffee, probably.
I'm on about six cups a day and I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.
Two glasses, sometimes three.
How do you feel about wine?
Easy.
It works for an hour.
I wake up at three anyway.
I know it's not helping.
You are noticing that clearly. That is useful.
Doesn't feel useful. Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.
I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.
What was it like to say today?
Strange.
Bit of relief actually.
Like grinning a bad weight and realize I was carrying.
What do you carry when you would like to put down first?
The nights, I think.
If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.
We can start, dear.
Did anything about your family growing up shape how you handled this?
My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire.
He never complained about anything. Not once.
That's the same. Just get on with it.
And you?
I'm the same. I keep thinking he would think as a week for being here.
What would he if he were here?
Then I'm not weak. Just very tired.
That sounds like something you could say to yourself as well.
Maybe. I don't know if I believe it yet.
That's fine. You don't have to. Let's think about what we could do between now and...
Would you be willing to try something small?
Depends how small. I haven't got much left.
Very small. Even for 20 minutes.
Very small.
What would actually happen in 20 minutes?
I think, probably, you wouldn't even notice.
Would you try it?
Yeah, half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire.
Do you know a sofa?
That sounds good. And a note of how the night goes?
I can do that.
Right when I wake up. If I wake up.
We're nearly out of time. How are you feeling really now?
Dired but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.
Very normal. It takes energy to say it loud, loud.
Thank you. I think I needed to hear that.
Same time next week?
Yeah, I'll be here.
I'll try to make it on time.
The trains are all full.
